correctness.rationale: At equilibrium P=1/delta, g=hY and r-1/(K delta)-delta Y=0. Hence every equilibrium produces Q=K delta(rh-delta g)-h=0. Since r=u_B+xg and delta=v_B+xh, the identity rh-delta g=u_Bh-v_Bg has degree at most two; Q degree <=4. Each x determines unique P,Y even at h=0. For the rational witness, the checker forms Q exactly and proves four disjoint sign changes with g/h>0 and delta>0 throughout each bracket. IVT gives four positive equilibria and degree four gives no more. Strict endpoint inequalities persist on an open parameter neighborhood. The proof makes the Q not-identically-zero assumption explicit.

originality.rationale: In the accessible full primary manuscript of Cruz and Neves (arXiv:2607.13281, Section 4) the positive equilibrium equation is described as fifth degree and examples have up to three positive coexistence equilibria. The common population-average structure yields the exact cancellation rh-delta*g=u_B*h-v_B*g, reducing the general nondegenerate bound to four, and four positive roots are certified by a new rational witness. A complete 2022 model text and the most relevant accessible published mathematical statements address coexistence conditions, local stability, a Hopf bifurcation, or a balanced special family, not this all-payoff sharp upper bound. Searches cannot establish historical uniqueness; the residual risks are explicit.
residual_risks: Unindexed older mathematical-ecology sources might contain the identical quartic cancellation or an equivalent four-equilibrium construction.
Full text of every potentially relevant unpublished manuscript was not exhaustively accessible; novelty remains a literature-bounded judgment rather than independent priority certification.
No claim is made that any of the four positive equilibria is locally stable or biologically observed.

value.rationale: The maximum number of positive, isolated coexistence states is a natural invariant of a three-species eco-evolutionary model. A general degree-four reduction narrows the equilibrium search beyond the original fifth-degree description; a strictly positive, robust four-state example attains that maximal complexity rather than merely re-evaluating a known case. It gives useful structural information independent of any yet-unproved stability analysis.
